purpose: Test whether coarse phase_like/amplitude_like labels describe the actual final-state phenomenology induced by the frozen RZ/RX/RY distortion mechanisms across circuit contexts.

decision_policy.PHENOMENOLOGICALLY_STABLE: Both coarse labels have overall expected-sign concordance >= 0.90; every eligible family/qubit/raw-label/strength stratum has expected-sign concordance >= 0.80; expected median dominance direction is correct for both labels; negligible fraction <= 0.10.
decision_policy.CONTEXT_DEPENDENT: Both coarse labels have overall expected-sign concordance >= 0.70, but at least one eligible context stratum violates the stable-stratum criterion or shows a direction reversal.
decision_policy.SEMANTICALLY_UNSTABLE: Either coarse label has overall expected-sign concordance < 0.70 or its median dominance direction is opposite the claimed phenomenology.
decision_policy.INSUFFICIENT_EFFECT: The negligible-effect fraction exceeds 0.10 such that the coarse phenotype is not physically resolved often enough for a stable label claim.

interpretation_rule: Injected mechanism labels (for example RZ drift versus RX/RY overrotation) remain distinct from observed-effect labels. A mechanism may be physically well-defined even if its final-state phenotype is context dependent.
